title: Dark Cloud
subtitle: A village carried in a stone
summary: Dark Cloud is Level-5's action role-playing game for PlayStation 2, first released in Japan on 14 December 2000. body: Dark Cloud is Level-5's action role-playing game for PlayStation 2, first released in Japan on 14 December 2000. After the Dark Genie destroys his village, Toan receives a magical stone that lets him recover what has vanished. He enters dungeons to find the people, buildings and belongings needed to rebuild the surface. This gives the adventure two connected activities: fighting through underground floors and arranging the community above them. A successful expedition brings back another piece of a place the player can gradually recognise as home.

The Georama system lets the player place recovered buildings and restore the objects around them. Residents also have requests about their surroundings, so rebuilding involves listening as well as choosing an attractive arrangement. A house placed in one position may satisfy someone who wants a particular neighbour or view. Returning from the dungeon changes the town, and talking to the people there supplies another reason to venture back underground. Recovery becomes visible in the streets rather than remaining a list of completed objectives in a menu.

Inside the dungeons, combat happens in real time and the party gradually gains characters with different weapons and abilities. Equipment develops through use and can be strengthened, making a familiar weapon something worth maintaining. Procedurally arranged floors offer new routes through repeated expeditions, although that repetition also drew criticism. Akihiro Hino directed the project at the young Level-5 studio, with music by Tomohito Nishiura. Its combination of dungeon exploration and reconstruction continued in Dark Chronicle, released in Japan in 2002 and known in North America as Dark Cloud 2.
